source_title: Mitie Group plc Annual Report and Accounts 2019
availability_evidence: The issuer-hosted annual report states on pages 50, 100 and 160 that the Strategic Report and financial statements were approved by the Board and authorised for issue on 5 June 2019; the PDF is preserved with its hash in the source index.
observation: A challenged, low-margin facilities-management market and labour-cost inflation created pressure, while average daily net debt increased to £302.0m. Mitie nevertheless increased revenue 9.4% to £2.2bn, operating profit before other items 6% to £88.2m and statutory operating profit to £50.2m from £1.1m; period-end net debt fell to £140.7m and leverage to 1.33x. Project Helix had already delivered about £45m of savings and Project Forte, including further consolidation and cost reductions, was already launched.
already_announced_exclusion: Project Helix, Project Forte, management delayering, back-office offshoring, organisational consolidation and associated cost reductions were announced or underway before cutoff and are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Sector and labour-cost pressure plus elevated average debt provide a contained signal, but strong revenue, profit, period-end debt and covenant metrics dominate; all identified restructuring programmes were already public.

source_title: Mitie Group plc Annual Report and Accounts 2021
availability_evidence: The issuer-hosted annual report states on pages 68, 144 and 206 that the Strategic Report and financial statements were approved by the Board and authorised for issue on 10 June 2021; the PDF is preserved with its hash in the source index.
observation: COVID-19 revenue mix and reduced project work lowered operating profit before other items to £63.4m from £86.1m and statutory operating profit to £8.3m. Group revenue increased to £2.56bn with the Interserve acquisition, the order book increased to £7.2bn and financing was strengthened through a £190m rights issue and refinanced £250m facility. Interserve integration synergies, Project Forte and related operational and headcount efficiencies were already announced and being implemented.
already_announced_exclusion: The Interserve integration and announced synergies, Project Forte, COVID operating adaptations, existing transformation charges and related efficiency actions were public or underway before cutoff and are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Pandemic disruption and the sharp fall in both adjusted and statutory operating profit warrant material pressure scores, moderated by the enlarged order book, strengthened financing and acquisition performance; known interventions are excluded.

source_title: Mitie Group plc Annual Report and Accounts 2023
availability_evidence: The issuer-hosted annual report states on pages 86, 150 and 208 that the Strategic Report and financial statements were approved by the Board and authorised for issue on 7 June 2023; the PDF is preserved with its hash in the source index.
observation: Inflation totalled £170m, free cash flow fell to £66m from £147m and average net debt rose to £84m from £25m, partly because invoice discounting was terminated. Mitie recovered £163m of inflation through repricing, delivered record £4.06bn revenue, increased underlying revenue 14%, achieved a 4.0% operating margin and maintained low leverage of 0.4x. Interserve headcount and procurement synergies and other margin-enhancement savings were already implemented or announced.
already_announced_exclusion: Interserve integration synergies, disclosed headcount reductions, procurement rationalisation, Forté and the existing margin-enhancement programme were announced or implemented before cutoff and are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Inflation and lower free cash flow create limited pressure, but near-complete cost recovery, record revenue, margin improvement, positive free cash flow and very low leverage provide strong contrary evidence.

source_title: NCC Group plc Annual Report and Accounts 2019
availability_evidence: The issuer-hosted annual report states on pages 91, 95 and 96 that the remuneration report, Directors' Report and responsibility statement were approved or signed on behalf of the Board on 24 July 2019; the PDF is preserved with its hash in the source index.
observation: Weaker UK demand, Escrow revenue decline and sales-resource challenges were present, but continuing revenue increased 7.6%, adjusted operating profit 9.4%, statutory operating profit 44.4% and profit before tax 52.1%. Cash conversion improved to 109.6% and net debt fell to £20.2m from £27.8m. The Securing Growth Together transformation and associated systems, organisation and performance-management changes were already active.
already_announced_exclusion: The Securing Growth Together transformation, sales-team changes, systems implementation and other disclosed organisational actions were announced or underway before cutoff and are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Local demand and Escrow execution pressure are credible but outweighed by broad profit growth, exceptional cash conversion and deleveraging; the transformation activity was already public.

source_title: NCC Group plc Annual Report and Accounts 2021
availability_evidence: The issuer-hosted annual report states on pages 125, 136 and 139 that the annual report and financial statements were approved or authorised for issue by the Board on 14 September 2021; the PDF is preserved with its hash in the source index.
observation: Pandemic disruption, talent attrition and a 2.4% Software Resilience revenue decline created contained divisional pressure. Group revenue increased 2.6% to £270.5m, adjusted operating profit rose 27.7% to £39.2m, statutory operating profit rose 37.3%, profit before tax rose 54.2% and free cash flow increased to £34.6m. Cash conversion remained 88.2%, and pre-acquisition underlying cash improved from £4.2m net debt to £12.6m cash. The Securing Growth Together transformation was already underway.
already_announced_exclusion: The Securing Growth Together transformation, cloud-system implementation, IPM acquisition activity and pandemic operating adaptations were announced or underway before cutoff and are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: The Software Resilience decline and recruitment pressure remain limited and are strongly offset by improving Group revenue, margins, profits, free cash flow and underlying net cash.

source_title: NCC Group plc Annual Report and Accounts 2023
availability_evidence: The issuer-hosted annual report states on pages 143, 155 and 159 that the Strategic Report and financial statements were approved or authorised for issue by the Board on 28 September 2023; the PDF is preserved with its hash in the source index.
observation: Delayed buying decisions and cancellations in North American technology and the UK reduced Cyber Security profitability sharply. Group gross margin fell to 39.4% from 42.1%, adjusted operating profit to £28.8m from £48.1m, and the Group recorded a £4.3m pre-tax loss and £49.6m net debt. Management disclosed difficult decisions, broad restructuring planning and FY24 cost efficiencies across Cyber Security and corporate functions. Those actions and the Manila delivery-centre plan were already announced by cutoff.
already_announced_exclusion: The broad business restructuring, Cyber Security and corporate cost efficiencies, Software Resilience operational review, new global delivery centre and related strategic actions were announced or planned before cutoff and are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: Severe demand, utilisation, margin, profit and debt deterioration creates a very strong underlying intervention signal, with limited offsets from Software Resilience growth and managed-services orders; the disclosed restructuring itself is excluded.

availability_evidence: The issuer-hosted annual report states on page 28 that the financial statements were approved and authorised for issue by the Board on 2 December 2019; the PDF is preserved with its hash in the source index.
observation: Yotta revenue declined slightly to £7.0m because of the completed SaaS transition and customer implementation delays, while Group gross margin eased to 71.2% from 72.4%. Group revenue nevertheless increased 11.7% to a record £35.3m, adjusted profit before tax increased 5.7% to £5.5m, operating cash generation rose to £7.7m and closing cash increased to £13.8m after dividends. Yotta's direct operations had already been reorganised.
already_announced_exclusion: The Yotta direct-operations reorganisation and completed SaaS-model transition were already undertaken before cutoff and are excluded from any future target event.
review_note: A small divisional revenue decline and slight gross-margin easing are decisively offset by record Group revenue, higher profit, stronger operating cash and increased closing cash.

availability_evidence: The issuer-hosted annual report states on page 30 that the financial statements were approved and authorised for issue by the Board on 1 December 2021; the PDF is preserved with its hash in the source index.
observation: Lockdowns, constrained location-based entertainment and supply-chain pressure affected trading, but every headline financial metric improved. Revenue increased to £35.6m from £30.3m, statutory profit before tax to £3.2m from £1.6m, adjusted profit before tax to £4.8m from £2.6m, operating cash generation to £14.5m from £7.0m and cash to £23.0m from £14.9m. Annual recurring revenue also increased and demand had recovered above pre-pandemic levels.
already_announced_exclusion: No qualifying restructuring or equivalent intervention had been announced by cutoff; pandemic working adaptations and ordinary growth-plan investment are excluded from the target definition.
review_note: Pandemic and supply-chain language provides a modest signal, but universal improvement across revenue, profit, recurring revenue, operating cash and cash balances supplies exceptionally strong contrary evidence.

availability_evidence: The issuer-hosted annual report states on page 33 that the financial statements were approved and authorised for issue by the Board on 4 December 2023; the PDF is preserved with its hash in the source index.
observation: Higher-cost components reduced gross margin to 65.0% from 67.5%, the order book normalised to £11.5m from £24.0m and net cash eased to £64.8m from £67.7m. Supply constraints had largely normalised and Group revenue increased 53.5% to a record £44.2m, adjusted profit before tax increased to £6.5m from £2.6m, continuing profit after tax increased to £5.7m from £3.4m and operating cash generation remained positive. Substantial net cash and growth investment provided strong resilience.
already_announced_exclusion: No qualifying restructuring or equivalent intervention had been announced by cutoff; the Yotta disposal, IVS acquisition, growth investment and supply-chain mitigation are excluded from the target definition.
review_note: Normalising orders and modest margin erosion create limited pressure, while record revenue, sharply higher profit, positive cash generation, resolved supply constraints and substantial net cash provide dominant offsets.
